Changed: A Call Tool response for a request run by a served /tool now shows the API's own response, with its status, as the main content. The tool-side details (method, URL, duration, size, request and response headers) moved into a separate collapsed "Tool details" section instead of the whole tool result being shown as one JSON blob.
Fixed: A failed tool call showed only "Tool reported an error" above the full raw result. It now shows a short "Tool call failed" card with the reason, a next-step hint for connection failures and timeouts, and the request that failed. If the API answered with an error body, that is still shown as the Response.

title: Fix: Failed Tool Calls Showed a Green OK

Fixed: A Call Tool response whose tool reported a failure (MCP's isError flag) still showed a green OK badge — only a small line inside the body hinted at the error. The badge now reads "Tool Error" in the error color.

title: Fix: False Incompatible Flag on 2.3.0 Betas

Fixed: The minimum app version was >=2.3.1, which incorrectly flagged every 2.3.0-beta.X build as incompatible even though the MCP tab work this plugin needs already landed by beta.2 — relaxed to >=2.3.0

title: Real OAuth Authorization, Not a Silent Failure

Added: An mcp-operation block connecting to an OAuth-protected server now shows a clear "This server requires authorization" state with an AUTHORIZE button next to Refresh, instead of a generic "couldn't discover capabilities" warning indistinguishable from a real outage.

Clicking AUTHORIZE drives a full, real OAuth 2.1 handshake automatically — discovery, Dynamic Client Registration, opening your real system browser to sign in, and completing the token exchange via a local loopback listener. No token to copy or paste manually.
Once authorized, the resulting token is reused automatically on every later request to that same server (transparently attached, never triggering a fresh browser popup on its own) until it expires.

Voiden itself is automatically brought back to the foreground the instant the browser hands control back — success or failure — instead of leaving the app in the background while a browser tab just says "you can close this tab now."
Fixed: A 401 from the server used to be silently indistinguishable from a real connection failure, both showing the same "server may be starting up or briefly unreachable" message.
Discovery's own status check was discarding the actual error detail on every failure — it bailed out on a synthetic status code before ever parsing the response body that carried it.

title: Docs: Skill Now Documents Singleton Block Rule

Fixed: The bundled skill.md now documents that mcp-connection is allowed at most once per request section. Previously undocumented, which could lead an AI agent to insert a second connection block instead of editing the existing one.

title: Initial Release
description: MCP client plugin for Voiden — connect to an external MCP server over HTTP and run an operation against it.

Added: MCP Connection block (/mcp-client) with a Server URL child and an Operation child
Support for list_tools, call_tool, list_resources, read_resource, list_prompts, get_prompt
Reuses the existing Auth block and assertions-table with no extra configuration
Connect to any Streamable-HTTP MCP server, including one running on localhost

Paste a Claude Desktop / Cursor / VS Code / Windsurf style mcpServers config (or VS Code's servers shape) to fill in the URL and headers automatically — every server in the config becomes its own block, not just the first
An mcp-remote bridge entry (npx -y mcp-remote <url> [--header ...]) unwraps into the real remote URL and headers directly, no local process spawned
Query Params and Path Params block support — resolved onto the server URL, same as REST requests
Request building goes through the same shared header/auth/cookie utilities voiden-rest-api uses, including inherited auth from .voiden-inherited.void ancestors
MCP responses render through the shared CodeEditor component — JSON syntax highlighting, search, and selection, with JSON-encoded text content auto-detected and pretty-printed
